builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted model uses more compute or memory than your workload can justify.
builder_plan.change: Check for a usable pruned checkpoint and runtime support before attempting model surgery.
builder_plan.baseline: The original unpruned model at the same precision, context, and load.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task quality, actual GPU memory, serving throughput, and preparation cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: An Asynchronous Federated Learning Platform for Lung Adenocarcinoma Grading via Foundation Models and Structural Pruning
summary: The method replaces centralized multi-institutional pathology training and full-weight federated transmission with a federated system (FedNova) that shares only pruned model weights, using UNI2 features with CLAM-SB. It costs the engineering complexity of operating a multi-client federated web platform and, for most aggregation algorithms, a degradation in Test AUC as pruning sparsity increases. It can fail when participating institutions have heterogeneous data distributions or small local cohorts, when the assumed privacy benefit is undermined by weight leakage, and when pruning interacts poorly with the chosen aggregation algorithm, as observed for FedAvg, FedProx, and FedBN.
rationale: The result is specific to multi-hospital histopathology collaboration, so the reader without federated infrastructure or clinical data partners should track it rather than adopt or test it now.
technique: Federated learning with structural pruning for pathology

claims.statement: The method replaces centralized multi-institutional pathology training and full-weight federated transmission with a federated system (FedNova) that shares only pruned model weights, using UNI2 features with CLAM-SB. It costs the engineering complexity of operating a multi-client federated web platform and, for most aggregation algorithms, a degradation in Test AUC as pruning sparsity increases. It can fail when participating institutions have heterogeneous data distributions or small local cohorts, when the assumed privacy benefit is undermined by weight leakage, and when pruning interacts poorly with the chosen aggregation algorithm, as observed for FedAvg, FedProx, and FedBN.

FedNova combined with 40% L1-norm structural pruning improved Test AUC across all sparsity levels, while FedAvg, FedProx, and FedBN showed decreasing Test AUC under pruning; no numeric AUC values are reported in the abstract.
